# Phase 5 — ablations

*Generated by `hydrocascade experiments` on 2026-09-24.*

> ### ⚠ Fitted on synthetic data
>
> `data_mode` is `synthetic` for `glofas`, `landslides`, and 9,764 of 9,765
> catalog rows are synthetic stand-ins. **Every parameter, every lead time and every
> p-value below describes the stand-in generators, not Kerala.** They exist to show
> the experimental machinery runs and that its diagnostics fire. Switching
> `data_mode` to `real` and rerunning turns all of them into results with no code change.


Doc 08 §3 calls this table *"the scientific core of the paper. It tells a reviewer exactly which of our ideas are real."* Each row removes exactly one component and refits everything else, so the change is attributable to that component alone.

**A component earns its place only if removing it makes held-out fit worse.** Where removing it changes nothing, that is reported as 'no detectable difference' rather than quietly dropped — Doc 08 §3: *"An idea that turns out not to matter is a finding."*

| # | removes | tests the claim | Δ train logL | Δ held-out logL | Δ AIC | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | cross terms (alpha_LF = alpha_FL = 0) | landslides raise flood risk | -163.85 | -187.99 | +319.7 | **earns its place** — removing it makes held-out fit worse |
| A2 | network kernel -> isotropic Euclidean | influence follows the drainage network | +766.30 | +718.72 | -1536.6 | **hurts** — the model is better without it |
| A3 | travel-time shift (tau = 0) | influence arrives as a wave, not instantly | +1760.15 | +1746.66 | -3522.3 | **hurts** — the model is better without it |
| A4 | runout connectivity gate | debris must physically reach a channel | -1.55 | -1.72 | -0.9 | no detectable difference — the data cannot distinguish these |
| A5 | dilution term (psi = 0) | effect weakens as the catchment grows | -0.00 | -0.10 | -2.0 | no detectable difference — the data cannot distinguish these |
| A6 | Part-1 background (mu constant in space) | the root-cause study improves the cascade model | -467.48 | -577.40 | +931.0 | **earns its place** — removing it makes held-out fit worse |
| A7 | rainfall windows | rainfall forcing matters | -1780.03 | -1810.80 | +3556.1 | **earns its place** — removing it makes held-out fit worse |
| A8 | mark term (eta = 0) | event size matters | -1.67 | -26.32 | -0.7 | **earns its place** — removing it makes held-out fit worse |
| A9 | mechanism mixture -> single exponential | mechanisms have distinguishable timescales | -1054.56 | -1201.34 | +2103.1 | **earns its place** — removing it makes held-out fit worse |

## The nested ladder M0-M5

These are nested, so likelihood-ratio tests apply. B1-B3 from Phase 3 are **not** nested and are compared on predictive metrics only — a likelihood-ratio test between a Hawkes model and XGBoost would be meaningless.

| model | includes | train logL | held-out logL | params | AIC | LR vs previous | df | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | constant rate per type | -61,879.28 | -71,561.05 | 2 | 123,762.6 | — | — | — |
| M1 | + susceptibility background, no time | -60,788.92 | -70,261.90 | 4 | 121,585.8 | 2180.73 | 2 | 0 |
| M2 | + rainfall windows — the honest baseline | -58,515.91 | -67,870.89 | 6 | 117,043.8 | 4546.01 | 2 | 0 |
| M3 | + self-excitation only (alpha_LF = alpha_FL = 0) | -56,662.45 | -65,976.97 | 11 | 113,346.9 | 3706.91 | 5 | 0 |
| M4 | + cross-excitation free | -56,625.36 | -65,940.90 | 13 | 113,276.7 | 74.18 | 2 | 7.798e-17 |
| M5 | + network kernel, travel time, mechanism mixture | -56,888.91 | -66,083.31 | 20 | 113,817.8 | -527.10 | — | **not nested** |

**M4 → M5 is not a nested step, so it carries no p-value.** M5 replaces the isotropic flood kernel with the network kernel — a change of kernel family, not an added parameter — so the chi-squared reference does not apply. Compare those two on held-out log-likelihood and AIC, which is also what ablation A2 and baseline B5 do.

**M0 is a genuine constant rate per type.** An earlier version had no way to switch self-excitation off, so M0–M2 all quietly included it and M3's 'first excitation' step was not one. The ladder is now nested as Doc 08 §2 describes.
